name: stone circles

attributes.attribute: sacred rings built by the Megalithic people
town built within one of Britain's largest circles
kept as homes of the Fairy race

sources: Harbison, Peter. *Pre-Christian Ireland: From the First Settlers to the Early Celts.* Thames and Hudson, 1988, 94.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Stone circles are a mythic site. Hundreds of them, from small to great, stand across the old Celtic lands. The Megalithic Civilization raised them thousands of years before the Celts appeared in written record. The rings of stone were kept sacred. The folk built their fields and towns around them but left the ring clear. At the town of Avebury in Britain, the town was built within the circle, which is among the largest in the land. There were times when the stones were moved or pulled down. In most places folk memory kept the circles whole, for the fairy race was said to live in such sites. The circles hold the heart of the beliefs of the old people of the land.
